## Dependents and concerns
- **No active-tab state exists.** The module tracks only `{next, tabs}`, so there was nothing to remap for the "active tab follows its tab" requirement. I did not add active-tab state. The nearest test finds a tab by title, because title is the only stable identity across a renumber. Any UI code outside this repo that holds an active key will break after a close, and `closeTab` returns no old-to-new mapping. Such code has to remap keys itself: a key above the closed one drops by 1, and a closed active tab needs its own fallback. Adding a mapping or an `active` field would be a follow-up.
- **No other keyed state in the repo.** I grepped for maps, persisted state and other uses of tab keys, and the only dependents were the README and header-comment examples, which I updated. No other `PRECEDENT.md` cites §stable-tab-keys.
- **The override does carry a real cost.** The old reason still holds:
  - **Remounting:** the key is the React key, so every tab to the right of a closed tab gets a new key. It remounts and loses scroll position and unsaved form input (the 2026-08-29 incident).
  - **URLs:** a `?tabs=` link or bookmark taken before a close points at different tabs afterwards.
  - I recorded both as accepted costs in §contiguous-tab-keys. If remount is a problem, the React `key` could come from a separate internal id, with `tN` used only for the URL. That would be a new design decision, so I left it out.
- **Closing an unknown key** no longer returns the tabs untouched. It still renumbers, which does nothing on contiguous state and normalises any gapped state that was passed in.
